headline: Google ties school Search access to accepting its AI tools
summary: Google announced new AI products for schools that let them disable some AI tools, such as Gemini, but schools that reject AI altogether lose access to Google Search, since AI is now built into the search engine. Outlets differ on how optional the AI really is, and Wired reports parents and educators worry it hurts children's learning.

claims.statement: Google announced new AI products for schools, letting them skip some AI tools but not remove AI from Search.

sources.quote: Google will let schools disable its AI tools, but not without sacrificing Search
Google will let schools skip AI tools, but they have to give up search, too
The search giant announced a slate of new AI products for classrooms and schools on Tuesday

claims.statement: Schools that ban AI entirely will lose access to Google Search.

sources.quote: Schools choosing to restrict AI altogether will no longer be able to access Google Search
Google says students in schools that ban AI won't have access to Search

claims.statement: AI remains built into Search itself even though schools can specifically skip Gemini.

sources.quote: Google: Schools can keep search while skipping Gemini, but AI search is non-negotiable
Google says there’s no way to use Search without using artificial intelligence

claims.statement: Wired reports parents and educators worry the policy leaves children less capable.

sources.quote: angering parents and educators who worry that easy, machine-generated answers are leaving kids less capable.

discrepancies.explanation: Early coverage described the AI/Search tie-up in neutral, technical terms, while later reporting frames the same policy more skeptically, as choice in name only.

quotes.quote: as AI features are now integrated into the search engine.
Google is technically offering schools more choice but not the choices anyone wants.
